summary: Alberta lookout near Whitecourt: 1938 radio station, 1952 and 1959 observers, 1953 steel tower replacement; provincial layer gives 2015 construction and active status.

facts.design: Earlier: smaller square lookout on a broad wooden tower base (Alberta Historic Places); 1953 steel tower; provincial layer lists type Steel
facts.status_note: Listed as active in the provincial layer; no source read describes the tower's physical condition today
facts.agency: Alberta Wildfire, under Agriculture and Forestry; forestry branch of the Alberta department of lands and mines in 1938

access.note: No public visiting arrangement found; sources describe a staffed working lookout. Provincial layer records access mode as drive.

staffing.status: staffed seasonally per Alberta's general description; last named observer found is Leo Goulet, appointed 1959

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1938 report places House Mountain in the Whitecourt district; the Canada Lookouts Alberta index lists it under the Slave Lake Division. The two sources use different unit names and the story reports both without choosing one.

notes_for_editor: Canada Lookouts is a compiled site that quotes newspapers and annual reports; its items are reproduced as quoted there and were not checked against originals. The provincial layer gives no unit for TOWER_HEIGHT (30.0 read as metres, per the brief). The brief's 'closed' access level and 'no public access' wording do not appear in any page read, so access is set to restricted for review. The 2015 year is the layer's YEAR_CONSTRUCTED field; no page read describes that work. 'Standing' rests on the layer's ACTIVE flag. A 1943 UCalgary photo of the House Mountain tower turned up in search, but the page returned HTTP 403, so no photo entry was added. The brief's 2015 'built' event is kept as the layer's value.
